newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tietmeyer warns against U.S. rate speculation.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer warns against U.S. rate speculation.

text.p: German central bank President Hans Tietmeyer Monday said markets should be cautious about expecting any further U.S. interest rate changes after the U.S. Federal Reserve raised rates on March 25.

"Of course we have to look at how markets will react, but one should be very cautious in expecting that this is the beginning of further moves, but of course it is all up to authorities in the U.S.," the Bundesbank chief said at a meeting of G-10 governors.
The Fed nudged its short-term fed funds rate up by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent, its first interest rate increase in over two years.

Tietmeyer said the governors also discussed market reaction to the U.S. Fed move, which raised fears of further rate hikes. But he said conditions on world financial markets now were different than in the 1994, when bond markets were sent into a tailspin, the last time the Fed tightened credit.
"All in all we see the situation as different from for example 1994 because capital market rates are more on solid ground and we don't see any excessive developments," he added.
The United States was represented by Fed Governor Lawrence Meyer, who was attending for the first time at the gathering held in the Basel-based Bank for International Settlements.
The G10 includes 11 countries -- Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands, Britain, Canada, Italy, Sweden, the United States, France, Japan and Switzerland.
